description: Machine-readable provenance for the VMC packet corpus. Every capture is assembled by adapters/liveCapture/vmc/tools/generate_packets.py from the OSC and VMC message shapes - there is no third-party capture data here and therefore no redistribution gate. Field values are measured from the committed files, never guessed.
limitations: Reproduces the shapes the protocol produces (bundled and unbundled frames, ignorable traffic, malformed datagrams, a bad message inside a good frame, a longer form of a known message, a duplicate, a backwards sender clock, a restart), not any particular sender application's quirks.
No real avatar is described: the rest offsets are invented proportions and the model message names a placeholder file.
Sender-application compatibility evidence is Milestone B's, recorded with the record tool from real senders and added here as it is measured.

captures.pins: The happy path: one OSC bundle per frame, a full torso rig including UpperChest, every rotation identity. The sender's clock starts at 12.5 s while the receive clock starts at 0, so an adapter that conflates the two cannot pass on this fixture alone.

The other sender shape: one message per datagram, spread across the frame interval, with the frame closed by a trailing /VMC/Ext/T rather than opened by a bundle. No UpperChest - a rig that does not solve it.

Well-formed traffic the body path does not implement: blend shapes, an HMD and controller transform, a camera, an option string. Unsupported is not malformed, and this is the fixture that holds the two diagnostics apart.

One datagram per packet-level refusal: empty, unterminated address, a type-tag string with no comma, a truncated argument, an unterminated string argument, a bundle element that overruns, an unaligned tail, and bytes that are not OSC at all - plus the two well-formed-but-unimplemented cases for contrast.

Well-formed OSC whose VMC arguments disagree with the protocol - the refusals the packet-level capture cannot reach, because every one of these decodes as OSC first. The load-bearing datagram is the second frame: one bone truncated to three floats inside an otherwise complete frame, so 'a bad message costs that message and not the frame' is pinned by a recorded session rather than only by a unit test.

Longer forms of known messages, which are not errors: a fourth integer on /VMC/Ext/OK, a third string on /VMC/Ext/VRM, six floats past /VMC/Ext/Root/Pos's quaternion, an argument on /VMC/Ext/Blend/Apply. It pins the shape - an argument is there and is counted, not read - and deliberately not a meaning for it, which no fixture in this repository is in a position to assert.

The arrival-order phenomena in one session: a byte-identical datagram delivered twice, a sender clock that goes backwards while arrival order does not, a frame that stops after six bones, and a restart that resets the sender clock to zero.
